Gastroenterologist

City Hospital
Main Road
Stillwater

21/02/2015

Dear Dr Thomas,
Re: Mr Patrick Newton,                                  D.O.B: 06/07/1989

Thank you for seeing Mr Newton, a 25-year-old accountant, whose features are suggestive of inflammatory
bowel disease. Your further management would be highly appreciated.

Mr Newton is single and lives with his parents. Unfortunately, he is a heavy smoker despite playing squash
regularly. Please note, he has a family history of Crohn's disease. He has had intermittent bilateral wrist
joint pain for the last six months.

On 21/02/2015, he presented to me complaining of a four-month history of chronic mild diarrhea together
with mild pain in the right lower quadrant of his abdomen. Moreover, he had a decreased appetite, the
reason why he lost a weight of three kilograms over the past four months. Although he tried diet
modification and taking ibuprofen, his symptoms persist. His examination was unremarkable except for a        Comment [teacher2]: took
generalised abdominal tenderness. His laboratory tests revealed an increase in the white cells count along
with a decrease in the red cells count and the haemoglobin. As well, his CRP and ESR were mildly elevated
in addition to a positive faecal occult blood test. The patient was advised to stop smoking.

In light of the above, the patent is being referred today for further assessment in order to rule out
inflammatory bowel disease. For any queries, please contact me.

Yours sincerely,

Doctor
